title: Devlog: Adding Dragons to the Game
author: alekblom
selftext: The process of adding creatures to the game is now as follows: generate an image of the model in Gemini, then take that image over to Tripo 3D for quickly generating a mesh, which is imported to Blender for manual rigging (if the Tripo 3D rig is good, I use that), then do some animations. Then I upload the GLB to the game, which uses a custom Claude-coded engine powered by Three.js. The game is live in pre-alpha at [sciasy.com](http://sciasy.com).

comments.author: Prior-Meeting1645
comments.body: Wow. Did u use the generate in parts feature? To have moving wings and mouth etc

replies.author: alekblom
replies.body: Nope, just made sure the image prompt included "mouth open". Anything off on the image making it hard to animate, just modify the image first, much easier than doing it manually in Blender at least.

comments.author: ScallionZestyclose16
comments.body: How’s the polycount, are you able to cap the outcome? Sounds interesting for sure!

replies.author: alekblom
replies.body: Yeah you cna set polycount in Tripo 3D. It didn't really want to go very low before (had to nudge it twice) but I think they now support lower polycounts and embraced the lowpoly style more. Been a few weeks since I generated with it so not exactly sure.
